title: Response path sampling and quantile KV metrics primer
content:
Purpose:
- Capture a compact, operational-ready set of metric names, trace anchoring rules, and sampling heuristics for response-path oriented investigations in tokenized inference.

Background and motivation:
- We often need to investigate tail latency and quality regressions that only reproduce for specific request paths: combinations of route, model version, prefix cache state, and client-config.
- Current dashboards show service-level quantiles and raw p50/p95 but lack a consistent way to slice by response path and to link sampled traces back to the exact prefix/kv state.
- This primer proposes metric definitions and a trace anchoring model to make investigations predictable and cheap.

Key definitions (naming conventions and intent):
- response_path_id: deterministic id computed at request start from route + model_version + route_config_hash + prefix_signature (if available). Used as a stable tag on metrics and sampled spans.
- inference.request.latency.quantile_ms: quantile histogram series (q50,q90,q95,q99) measured at request completion, labeled by response_path_id, model, route, tenant.
- inference.kv.prefix_hit_rate: fraction of requests that found a relevant prefix entry (per response_path_id). Aggregateable over time windows.
- inference.kv.kv_lookup_count: number of KV lookups per request (helps detect pathological prefix churn).
- inference.batch.size_distribution: histogram of batch sizes at dispatch; used with latency quantiles to show batching impact per path.
- inference.response.size_tokens: token count output (useful to normalize latency per token).

Trace anchoring model (how to tie spans to metrics):
- Anchor span tags at request start: span tag response_path_id, model=, route=, prefix_present=true/false, cache_key_hash (first 8 chars).
- Root span name: inference.request:request_id. Child spans include kv.lookup, batching.wait, model.encode, model.decode, streaming.write.
- For KV cache hits, emit an explicit span kv.lookup with tags hit=true/false and latency_ms. This enables counting cache hit latency in waterfall views.
- Sampling decision: made after root span completes and after computing latency; supports backfilling with low-overhead logs that reference response_path_id when traces suppressed.

Sampling heuristics (recommended to control cost and surface tail behavior):
- Baseline sampling: 0.5% of requests across all tenants for full traces.
- Adaptive tail sampling: sample 100% of requests with latency > dynamic_threshold (initial default 2.5x p95) or errors.
- Path-focused boost: when a response_path_id shows a 2x rise in error rate or a 20% jump in q95 within a sliding window, increase sampling for that path to 10% for 1 hour.
- Prefix-change capture: if prefix_signature changes for a tenant, temporarily sample 5% of requests for that tenant for 30 minutes to observe fallout.
- Cost guardrails: cap total trace volume per cluster; prefer recording kv.lookup spans and lightweight root spans when full spans would exceed budget.

Dashboard composition suggestions:
- Landing panel: top table of response_path_id by q95 delta (last 1h vs baseline 7d) + counts + kv prefix_hit_rate. Provide quick link to trace explorer filtered by response_path_id.
- Heatmap: latency quantile heatmap by hour and response_path_id cardinality capped (show top N paths by traffic).
- Distribution panel: token-normalized latency (ms per output token) histograms, with batch size overlay.
- KV telemetry: prefix_hit_rate over time, per-tenant and global; kv_lookup_count distribution.
- Trace sampling telemetry: sampled rate per path and estimated unsampled tail coverage (approx using sampled quantiles).
- Alert widgets: q95 increase > 30% sustained 10m for any response_path_id with traffic > 100 reqs/day; prefix_hit_rate drop > 15% in 10m.

Investigation workflow (playbook snippets):
- Step 0: reproduce signal on dashboard; note response_path_id, model, route, tenant.
- Step 1: open trace explorer filtered to response_path_id and time window; look for kv.lookup spans and batching.wait hotspots.
- Step 2: compare batch.size_distribution and response.size_tokens to detect workload shifts.
- Step 3: if trace scarcity, trigger temporary path-focused sampling (see sampling heuristics) or request a debug trace from customer (if private deployment).
- Step 4: if prefix_signature changed, correlate with deploy timeline and prefix rollout tickets.

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- How to compute response_path_id deterministically while keeping PHI/PII out of tags? Propose hashing with salted cluster key and only keeping 8-char prefix.
- Cardinality limits: top-N approach hides low-volume paths where bugs surface. Need a cheap low-cardinality anomaly detector to surface emerging paths.
- Cost vs fidelity: do we prefer more kv.lookup spans sampled at high rate or fewer full traces? Early experiments favor kv spans + root sampling as high signal/cost ratio.

Next steps (action items):
- (Ethan) prototype response_path_id library in telemetry common lib and open PR (linked).
- (Maya) add q95/q99 quantile metrics to the agent metric set and sketch dashboard wireframe.
- (Sofia) run a 2-week sampling experiment on canary cluster with adaptive tail sampling enabled and report trace volume delta.

Appendix: suggested metric names for implementation (stable strings)
- inference.request.latency.quantile_ms{quantile=[0.5,0.9,0.95,0.99], tags=[response_path_id,model,route,tenant]}
- inference.kv.prefix_hit_rate{tags=[response_path_id,tenant]}
- inference.kv.lookup_latency_ms{tags=[response_path_id,hit]}
- inference.batch.size_histogram{tags=[model,route]}
- inference.response.tokens{tags=[response_path_id]}

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally implementation pragmatic rather than perfect; aim is to get an MVP that enables fast investigations. Expect revisions after the canary sampling run.
